## Which Colombia tours include El Peñon de Guatape?

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring [El Peñon de Guatape](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) in the main itinerary. The monolith in Antioquia rises around 220 metres above the surrounding area. Nearby is a reservoir with intricate shorelines and green islets, while a few kilometres away lies [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/) with its painted house facades.

On our tours, this is **a day trip from Medellin**, returning to the city for the night. The main question when choosing a package is therefore not accommodation next to the rock but how [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/) combines with the rest of Colombia. El Peñon appears on different days:

| Tour | Day of rock visit |
|---|---|
| [Colombia in 7 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) | Day 4: Medellin and Guatape |
| [Colombia in 9 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) | Day 6: after the coffee region |
| [Colombia in 11 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) | Day 10: before flying home |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_colombia_highlights_7_days,tour_colombia_explorer_9_days,tour_colombia_complete_11_days}}

In each case, the [“Guatape and El Peñon Rock from Medellin” excursion](/colombia/medellin/guatape-rock-and-town-from-medellin/) provides the central experience: Guatape's streets, the monolith and views over the reservoir. Costs, transfers and guide languages depend on the specific programme; inclusion in this catalogue alone does not define which services have been paid for.

## Differences between the 7-, 9- and 11-day programmes

### 7 days: Bogota, Medellin and Cartagena

The [“Colombia in 7 Days: Bogota, Medellin and Cartagena”](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) itinerary offers a first introduction to the country's main contrasts. In [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), the programme covers the historic centre, museums and surrounding attractions before continuing to Medellin. The rock and Guatape are scheduled for day 4, and the journey ends in [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) with a day near the Rosario Islands.

This is the shortest of the three itineraries. It does not include a separate extended stay in the Quindio coffee region, but does combine the Andes, urban experiences and Caribbean coast. Flights are paid for separately; scheduled excursions and private transfers are among the included services.

### 9 days: cities, coffee and the Caribbean

[“Colombia in Four Chapters”](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) adds the coffee region to the cities. After Bogota, travellers head to [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), see [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and [El Ocaso Farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/), and then continue to Medellin.

Guatape and El Peñon feature on day 6. The route then moves to Cartagena and the sea. Two nights in each of four cities create a more even alternation between city tours, mountain scenery and the coast. A separate active day in the coffee region includes ziplining and horseback riding. International and domestic flights are not included in the price of this tour.

### 11 days: coffee region, San Andres and Guatape

[“Many Faces of Colombia: 11 Days from Bogota to the Caribbean”](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) is designed as a longer journey. In addition to Bogota, Salento, Cocora Valley and a coffee farm, it features Cartagena and [San Andres Island](/colombia/place/san-andres/). After the island section, the route continues to Medellin, with the rock visit near the end on day 10.

This tour is private. Domestic flights are paid for separately, and island accommodation arrangements differ from those in the cities. Before booking, confirm the final number of nights: the tour description contains a discrepancy between its itinerary and hotel sections, which needs to be resolved in the quotation.

**The choice is straightforward:** the seven-day option suits an initial introduction with limited time; the nine-day trip adds coffee and activities; the eleven-day journey combines the coffee region, island relaxation and Medellin.

## What makes the rock excursion special?

The rock, also known as La Piedra del Peñol, is a massive granite formation overlooking the reservoir. Its origins are linked to the geology of the Antioquia Batholith and long-term erosion of surrounding rock. Its near-vertical face is imposing from below, while views from the top take in reservoir arms and islets.

The reservoir itself is man-made. This part of Antioquia is associated with a major hydroelectric project that transformed the area around Guatape. The landscape therefore combines a natural rock formation with an artificial waterscape. Walking around the town offers a chance to discover more about the region's history.

Guatape's houses have a characteristic feature called **zócalos**, bright relief panels along the lower facades. They depict animals, plants, local occupations and scenes. After the expansive views from the rock, walking through the narrow streets offers a completely different introduction to Antioquia.

If El Peñon itself is your main goal, consider a [standalone excursion from Medellin](/colombia/medellin/guatape-rock-and-town-from-medellin/) without a multi-day tour. It is convenient if you are already staying in the city; the larger packages are for visitors who want to connect this site with other Colombian regions.

## Climbing the rock and physical demands

A long staircase leads to the summit. The ascent involves **many consecutive steps** and can be tiring in hot or humid weather. Tourist descriptions differ in the number of steps, so it is better to judge the effort by the nature of the climb rather than by one figure. If you have knee, breathing or mobility difficulties, discuss adapting the excursion in advance.

An important distinction is that **a stop at the rock does not automatically guarantee a climb to the top**. Our programmes include visiting the monolith and enjoying panoramic scenery, but entrance payment, whether an ascent is required and practical arrangements must be checked for the specific offer. If agreed beforehand, some travellers may instead admire the rock from below and walk around Guatape.

For the day trip, bring comfortable shoes, water, sun protection and a light rain layer. Weather changes in the Andes, and the exposed viewing area differs from Medellin's sheltered streets. Account for travel time in both directions, since the excursion returns to the city.

## Where to place Guatape in a longer itinerary

The El Peñon excursion is planned in the Medellin region, separately from Bogota and the Caribbean coast. On the seven-day programme, it falls midway through the journey; on the nine-day one, after two nights in the coffee region; on the eleven-day one, near the end. This positioning affects fatigue and the number of subsequent transfers.

If you mainly want to combine views from the rock with culture, a trip from Medellin is enough. If you also want to see coffee plantations and wax palms, compare the nine- and eleven-day options featuring [El Ocaso Farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/) and [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/). For more itineraries, see the [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/) or [adventure tours in Colombia](/interests/adventure/tours/colombia/).

Exact ascent hours, access after heavy rain and entrance rules depend on current attraction operations. Check them closer to the trip. Do not count staircase time as an unconditional part of the itinerary unless the ascent has been confirmed.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting El Peñon

### Are El Peñon Rock and Guatape town the same place?

No. [El Peñon de Guatape](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) is a rocky monolith with a viewpoint, while [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/) is a separate town known for painted houses and its waterfront. Ada Tours combines them in a day excursion from Medellin.

### Do you need to stay overnight in Guatape?

On all three itineraries, the overnight stay is in [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/) and the rock is visited during the day. Accommodation by the reservoir would be a different travel arrangement to discuss separately.

### Is the staircase climb included in the tour price?

The published programmes confirm a rock visit, but the detailed terms for summit access must be checked in the chosen offer. Do not equate a stop at El Peñon with a paid ascent unless explicitly stated.

### How do you choose between 7, 9 and 11 days?

Look at the remaining destinations. The [seven-day tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) covers cities and the Caribbean; the [nine-day one](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) adds the coffee region; the [eleven-day one](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) adds San Andres Island as well. All three include the rock.

### Can you visit the rock without booking a longer tour?

Yes. Ada Tours offers a separate [“Guatape and El Peñon Rock from Medellin” excursion](/colombia/medellin/guatape-rock-and-town-from-medellin/), without a journey through several regions of Colombia.

## Filandia, Colombia: colourful streets, crafts and Quindio views

**Filandia is a small town in Colombia's coffee region, worth visiting for its streets and local culture.** Brightly painted facades stand beside wooden balconies, cafes, workshops and streets best explored without a rigid schedule. The town sits among the green hills of Quindio Department.

Filandia fits well into a trip near [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/), but the two places have distinct atmospheres. Salento is often a base for visiting [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/). Filandia suits a slower day in town, panoramic views and discovering craft traditions.

## Walking through the historic streets

Start at the main square and surrounding blocks. Many houses have brightly painted facades, while carved balconies, doors and timber details illustrate the coffee region's architectural traditions. It is best to explore on foot, noticing small shops, courtyards and everyday town life.

Filandia's architecture belongs to the wider cultural landscape of Colombia's coffee districts, where farming, small towns and local craftsmanship developed together. Filandia is also a living community, with ordinary businesses operating alongside tourist shops.

If you want to learn more, make time to speak with a local guide or craftsperson. It is an easy way to understand the purpose of architectural details and discover which traditional crafts continue today.

## Quindio viewpoint

One of Filandia's notable attractions is **Colina Iluminada**, a viewpoint often called the Quindio lookout. It stands on a hill and overlooks the surrounding landscape: coffee-growing hills, small settlements and distant mountain ridges.

The panorama depends on the weather. Rain and cloud can limit visibility, so on a busy itinerary it helps to allow some flexibility in the order of stops. Check current admission arrangements and opening conditions for the viewpoint in advance.

Filandia's ordinary streets are excellent for photographs too: colourful facades and balconies offer an entirely different subject from the natural scenery of Cocora Valley.

## Crafts and coffee-region culture

Filandia is known for workshops using local materials, including woven and basketry products. Its craft traditions are rooted in rural life and everyday needs. Pay attention to how objects are made, what they are used for and the maker's story, not just the finished souvenir.

Coffee is also part of daily life here. You can sample different preparations and discover regional food. However, tasting coffee in a cafe and touring a working plantation are different activities. To learn about growing and processing beans, dedicate time to a separate farm around [Armenia](/colombia/place/armenia/) or [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/).

## Filandia or Salento: which should you choose?

| If your priority is | Choose |
|---|---|
| Historic streets and workshops | Filandia |
| Access to the palms of Cocora Valley | Salento |
| Coffee estates and a transport base | Armenia |

You do not have to choose just one. Both towns can fit into a trip around Quindio, but make time to explore each rather than spending the whole day travelling between them.

If your nature programme includes a long hike through [Cocora's](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) cloud forest, place Filandia on a different day or after a short walking route. This gives you more variety and avoids rushing the viewpoint.

## How much time is needed?

**A few hours** are sufficient for central streets, a cafe and the viewpoint if transport is arranged in advance. **A full day** allows for a craft workshop and a leisurely lunch without reducing the town to a series of brief stops.

When choosing accommodation, compare Filandia, Salento and [Armenia](/colombia/place/armenia/) against your actual itinerary. If most of the trip involves coffee farms and transfers, a town with good transport connections may be most convenient; to stay longer in a small town, consider available services and evening travel.

## Weather and practical advice

Altitude and humidity make the coffee region's weather changeable. Bring a light rain layer and comfortable shoes for sloping streets. Popular areas may be busier on weekends and public holidays, so plan a relaxed walk at an appropriate time.

On a longer trip, Filandia can be combined with [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/) and other coffee-region destinations. We can help coordinate towns, farms and natural areas based on actual driving times. Suitable trips are available in the [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/), with [coffee-focused journeys](/interests/coffee-tours/) grouped separately.

## Frequently asked questions about Filandia

### How is Filandia different from Salento?

Filandia is known for architecture, crafts and its viewpoint. Salento is especially convenient for a visit to Cocora Valley. Both belong to the same coffee region.

### Can you see Filandia in half a day?

Yes. That is often enough for the central streets and viewpoint if transport is organised in advance. Workshops and a relaxed visit take longer.

### Where is the best panorama in Filandia?

The best-known spot is the Colina Iluminada viewpoint. In clear weather it offers views over the Quindio hills; check visiting arrangements before travelling.

## Which Ada Tours itinerary visits Filandia?

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring [Filandia](/colombia/place/filandia/) on the main route. The town lies in Quindio Department amid Colombia's coffee-growing hills. Its bright facades, wooden balconies, square and surrounding views complement the area's better-known natural attractions.

On the current [“Colombia Live”](/colombia/tour/colombia-live/) programme, Filandia is scheduled for **day 5**. The excursion leaves [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), visits Filandia, then continues to [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/). The overnight stay remains in Pereira: Filandia is a cultural stop and walking visit, not a separate accommodation base.

| Detail | “Colombia Live” |
|---|---|
| Duration | 13 days |
| Filandia | Day 5 |
| Regional base | Pereira |
| Also on that day | Cocora and Salento |
| Onward destinations | Santa Marta, Tayrona, Cartagena |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_kolumbiya_live}}

The programme introduces different parts of the country in sequence. The [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/) helps compare it with shorter trips that spend less time in the coffee region or do not include Filandia at all.

## What you will see in Filandia on day 5

After breakfast, the day begins with a drive from Pereira. Guests first walk through Filandia's streets, with colonial houses and painted wooden balconies. They then visit the **Quindio viewpoint** overlooking the region's green hillsides and settlements.

The next part of the stop introduces local food: drinks and desserts at a Filandia restaurant are included. It is an enjoyable way to experience the town without rushing, spend more time on its main streets and appreciate the difference between a small coffee-region town and larger Pereira.

The route then heads to [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/). Both the scenery and excursion subject change: instead of town facades, there are cloud forests, wax palms and a walk with an eco-guide. After the nature section, travellers visit [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and its colonial streets.

The entire excursion day lasts **approximately 7 hours**. Confirmed inclusions are private transport, an English-speaking guide, the food experience in Filandia, specified admissions and a typical lunch. The exact stops and viewpoint availability depend on the travel date; check current visiting arrangements before departure.

## Filandia, Salento and Cocora: three distinct experiences

These places share a coffee-growing region but offer different experiences.

| Place | Why visit |
|---|---|
| [Filandia](/colombia/place/filandia/) | Balconies, viewpoint, cuisine |
| [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) | Streets and craft workshops |
| [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) | Wax palms and cloud forest |

Filandia is on a hill and is known for panoramic views. Official tourism resources for Quindio highlight its wooden Colina Iluminada lookout tower and the historic buildings around the main square. The town retains a tradition of wooden architectural elements and brightly painted facades.

Salento is also in the coffee region, but its purpose on this route is different: the walk through historic streets follows the Cocora Valley visit. The valley reveals the natural surroundings of these rural towns: tall palms, mountain trails and cloud forest. Combining all three stops makes the day varied without visiting several coffee estates at once.

Travellers primarily interested in architecture and cultural traditions may find Filandia especially appealing. If longer nature walks matter more, you may prefer to spend additional time in Cocora. Tell us which part of the day has priority when booking so we can discuss possible adjustments to the schedule.

## Filandia within the thirteen-day journey

[“Colombia Live”](/colombia/tour/colombia-live/) begins in [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) with the historic centre and a coffee tasting. The route then covers Zipaquira and [Villa de Leyva](/colombia/place/villa-de-leyva/), with colonial architecture and nearby natural attractions. Day 4 includes an airport transfer in Bogota and a flight to Pereira; airfare is listed among separately payable expenses.

Travellers spend several days in Pereira. **Filandia, Salento and Cocora make up day 5**, while the next day is devoted to an interactive coffee-production programme around [Santa Rosa de Cabal](/colombia/place/santa-rosa-de-cabal/). These excursions have different purposes: Filandia introduces a town and its food, while the coffee farm focuses on bean production.

After the coffee region, the itinerary heads to the Caribbean, [Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/) and [Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/), ending in [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The thirteen-day tour thus suits visitors who want to combine culture, mountain scenery, nature and the coast in one journey. If you are interested only in the coffee region, this complete itinerary may be more than you need.

Assess inclusions and price against the [tour page](/colombia/tour/colombia-live/). The package includes scheduled transfers, accommodation and meals in the specified quantities, and excursions with an English-speaking guide. International and domestic airfares are excluded. Do not assume all standalone Colombia excursions are part of this particular route.

## How this differs from a tour visiting El Ocaso

There are different ways to learn about coffee growing in the region. Other Ada Tours trips, for example, visit [El Ocaso Farm near Salento](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/), where guests see the production process and taste coffee. In “Colombia Live”, the separate coffee programme takes place **around Santa Rosa de Cabal**, while Filandia is scheduled as its own town stop.

These programmes should not be treated as identical merely because they visit Quindio and involve coffee. The farms, routes, durations and onward destinations differ. If your priority is El Ocaso itself, consult [tours including that farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/tour/). For coffee-region towns within a wider journey through the Andes and Caribbean, compare the actual “Colombia Live” itinerary.

More options by theme appear under [coffee tours](/interests/coffee-tours/) and [Colombia food and wine trips](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/colombia/). A cultural and historical focus is also available in [Colombia culture itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/). These catalogues allow comparisons by activities rather than one word in a title.

## What to prepare for

Filandia sits on hills, while walking sections are planned in nearby Cocora Valley. The full excursion day calls for comfortable shoes, clothes for changeable mountain weather and rain protection. Even with most transfers by vehicle, the day includes outdoor stops and walking.

The programme combines a town visit, restaurant, viewpoint and nature trail. Tell us in advance if anyone in your group has difficulty walking for long periods or using stairs. You can clarify which parts are essential and where a gentler pace may be possible; specific adjustments are confirmed when arranging the trip.

Colombia's Coffee Cultural Landscape was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2011. It embraces not a single plantation but a combination of farmland, small towns and traditions of coffee growing on Andean slopes. Filandia shows the urban side of this culture. Exploring it alongside rural and natural sites is what makes the excursion day so varied.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Filandia

### Is Filandia part of the main itinerary or an optional stop?

On [“Colombia Live”](/colombia/tour/colombia-live/), Filandia is included on day 5 together with Salento and Cocora Valley. It is a core part of the route, not an optional add-on.

### Do you need to spend the night in Filandia?

The published programme provides overnight stays in Pereira. Filandia is visited on a day excursion, after which travellers return to their base in the coffee region.

### Will the same trip include a coffee farm?

Yes. A separate day of “Colombia Live” is devoted to coffee production around Santa Rosa de Cabal. **This is not El Ocaso Farm**, which has its own [excursion](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) and other tours.

### How long does Filandia, Cocora and Salento take together?

The tour description allocates about 7 hours to the combined excursion day. This refers to the whole programme, not only the walk in Filandia. Individual stop durations depend on how the day is organised.

### Is the tour suitable for a first visit to Colombia?

Yes, if you want to see several regions in one trip and are comfortable with a busy programme and transfers. It combines Bogota, Villa de Leyva, the coffee region, Santa Marta, Tayrona and Cartagena. For a shorter holiday, compare [other Colombia itineraries](/colombia/tour/).

## Fusagasuga, Colombia: coffee plantations near Bogota

[Fusagasuga](/colombia/) is a town in Cundinamarca Department south of [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/). It often features in trips designed to introduce visitors to local farming and coffee culture. The main stop on our itineraries is [Hacienda Coloma coffee estate](/colombia/place/hacienda-coloma/), where guests can follow the journey from the coffee plant to the finished cup.

According to the estate, it is approximately **70 km from central Bogota**. The drive takes longer than the map distance might suggest, due to leaving the capital, mountain roads and stops. One of our current programmes allows around **120 minutes each way**. This is a guide for that itinerary, not a guaranteed travel time for every trip.

## What to see in Fusagasuga

A visit to Fusagasuga is particularly interesting for travellers who want to see Colombia beyond its major cities. Instead of a museum in central Bogota, you can visit a working estate where coffee plants grow, cherries are harvested and beans prepared for roasting.

### Hacienda Coloma: from coffee seed to cup

At [Hacienda Coloma](/colombia/place/hacienda-coloma/), visitors learn about successive stages of coffee production. The tour starts with seeds and young plants, then continues among coffee bushes. Arabica is cultivated at the estate, including under the shade of taller trees. The guide explains how cherries are picked and why subsequent processing influences the drink's flavour.

At the processing area, you can learn about removing pulp, washing, drying and sorting beans. Hulling, roasting and brewing follow. The visit ends with an introduction to the finished drink. The entire process is particularly clear when you see **the fruit, the unroasted bean and the finished cup on a single estate**.

The estate's colonial architecture, gardens of flowering plants and shady trees complement the tour. An interest in food and local culture is enough for this experience: a strenuous trek or specialist preparation is not usually required for a standard plantation visit.

### Coffee and rum: different parts of the experience

Coloma is also known for rum with coffee notes. The producer offers a separate introduction to rum and a tasting, distinct from the basic coffee tour and potentially subject to its own terms and price.

On the current [ten-day Colombia journey with a coffee tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-coffee-10-days/), **day 2** includes the coffee estate and a cellar visit with rum tasting. These are the terms of that specific tour. If visiting the estate independently, choose your preferred format rather than assuming rum tasting is included with every coffee excursion.

## Organising a trip from Bogota

Fusagasuga works as a day trip from the capital, returning to the city. You can combine the drive, a plantation tour and an introduction to local products, then return to Bogota in the evening.

When choosing a programme, check transfer time, guide language and included activities. The label "coffee tour" can sometimes mean only a walk around a plantation and sometimes the complete production cycle with additional tastings. Compare **specific stops and terms**, not merely the general subject.

To compare options, visit [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) and [coffee journeys](/interests/coffee-tours/). On a longer route, Bogota might be the starting point before continuing to [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/) and the Caribbean coast. That is a different experience from spending several days at a coffee estate.

## Fusagasuga and Colombia's Coffee Region: what is the difference?

Colombia has a famous Coffee Region, often associated with Pereira, Manizales and Armenia. Fusagasuga lies in another part of the country, closer to Bogota. A trip to Coloma offers an introduction to coffee production without a separate long transfer to the Coffee Region.

The choice depends on your goal. If you want to see the plants, learn about processing beans and taste coffee in one day, Fusagasuga is a good addition to a capital visit. Exploring several estates, mountain towns and coffee valleys requires more days and a different itinerary.

## When to visit and what to bring

Coffee estates can be visited in different seasons. Demonstrations of certain farming activities, however, depend on the current growing and processing cycle. Do not expect every harvesting stage to take place on every day of the year.

Closed non-slip shoes, a light rain jacket and sun protection are useful on outdoor paths. Bring water and allow time for the return drive. The logistics should fit your stay in Bogota and any subsequent flights.

## Frequently asked questions about Fusagasuga

### Where is Fusagasuga?

It is in Cundinamarca Department, south of [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/). The surrounding area is home to Hacienda Coloma, known for tours of coffee production.

### What makes a Hacienda Coloma excursion interesting?

Visitors discover coffee cultivation, harvesting and processing beans, roasting and brewing. It is a practical way to understand Colombian coffee production.

### Do you have to stay overnight in Fusagasuga?

No. The [ten-day Ada Tours programme](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-coffee-10-days/) visits Coloma on a dedicated excursion day departing from Bogota. Other possibilities depend on your chosen accommodation and itinerary.

### Is rum tasting always included in a coffee tour?

No. It is a separate service offered by the estate. Check the precise itinerary; the cited Ada Tours tour does include a cellar visit.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Fusagasuga in their main itinerary. Both programmes continue to other parts of Colombia. Choose based on **the complete journey**, not merely the coffee-farm excursion: after Bogota, the route continues to Medellin and the Caribbean coast.

### What happens on the coffee day?

On the [ten-day Colombia tour featuring a coffee excursion](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-coffee-10-days/), the visit to Hacienda Coloma takes place on day 2. It is approximately a two-hour drive from Bogota to Fusagasuga. On the estate, guests discover coffee production from seeds and plant cultivation to harvesting, processing and brewing. The coffee visit is followed by a tasting of rum with coffee notes and a traditional regional lunch, before returning to Bogota. A Russian-speaking guide accompanies travellers that day.

The [nine-day “Bogota, Medellin and Cartagena” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-9-days/) also visits the estate on day 2. Guests learn about planting, harvesting, processing and roasting beans, taste coffee and eight-year-aged rum and have lunch before the return drive. This is a full excursion stop, not a brief shopping visit.

On both itineraries, visiting Fusagasuga takes **one part of a wider trip through Colombia**, with the overnight stay after the excursion in Bogota. Neither programme provides for a separate multi-day stay in the town.

## Fusagasuga or Colombia's Coffee Region: which to choose?

Fusagasuga suits people departing from Bogota who want to discover coffee without another transfer and overnight stay near Pereira. At Hacienda Coloma, you can experience the main stages of processing beans at one working estate. According to the estate, its coffee tour includes a nursery, Arabica plantings, processing facilities, sorting, roasting and tasting.

A different format is a tour of the coffee belt, visiting [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and [El Ocaso coffee farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/). It places more emphasis on several towns, landscapes and the culture of a whole region. Do not assume these stops are included in a tour passing through Fusagasuga: these are different places and a different type of trip.

Find coffee-focused choices under [Coffee Tours](/interests/coffee-tours/) and compare complete country routes in the [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/).

## How the trip from Bogota is organised

Hacienda Coloma is in the Fusagasuga area. On our chosen programmes, the drive from Bogota takes approximately two hours each way; actual time depends on the road and traffic. The excursion day covers both the estate visit and return to the capital. Allow **most of the day** rather than scheduling another time-sensitive excursion immediately afterwards.

A city tour of Bogota, a trip to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and a visit to [Zipaquira](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) occupy separate days on these itineraries. This division allows more time for each activity. Treating Coloma as an en-route stop on the way to Guatavita would misrepresent the programme's geography.

If travelling independently, check the estate's visiting conditions, tour language and booking requirements separately. The estate's standalone tour and the inclusions of a selected Ada Tours package are different arrangements.

## Who is this kind of itinerary for?

**Coffee lovers.** You can observe the real process: plants, green beans, processing, roasting and the finished drink. Even experienced coffee enthusiasts can learn what influences aroma and flavour by visiting the estate.

**First-time visitors to Colombia.** One journey combines [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), a coffee day, [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). You experience the contrast between a high-altitude capital, a working estate, a modern major city and the Caribbean coast.

**Travellers who prefer an organised programme.** You can compare excursion days and transfers in advance instead of assembling several disconnected day trips from different cities. Exact inclusions still depend on the selected tour, not on the general title of the catalogue.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Fusagasuga

### Can you visit a coffee plantation without travelling to Pereira?

Yes. Hacienda Coloma is in Fusagasuga, which Ada Tours programmes visit on a dedicated day trip from Bogota. You can explore coffee production without travelling to the coffee region around Pereira.

### How long does it take to reach Fusagasuga?

Both current nine- and ten-day itineraries give an estimate of around two hours each way from Bogota. Allow a substantial part of the day for the excursion and return.

### Is Hacienda Coloma included in both tours compared here?

Yes. It is on both itineraries: the [nine-day](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-9-days/) and [ten-day](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-coffee-10-days/) programmes. Check each tour's description for the precise tastings and other services.

### Is there an overnight stay in Fusagasuga?

Both programmes return to Bogota after the estate visit. Neither specifies a separate overnight stay at the coffee farm.

### What else can you see on the same trip?

Both programmes combine the coffee day with Bogota's attractions, [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), [Zipaquira](/colombia/place/zipaquira/), [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/) and finally [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/).
